units.zh: 孝昭皇帝演，字延安，神武皇帝第六子，文宣皇帝之母弟也。
units.en: Emperor Xiaozhao, whose personal name was Yan and style name Yan'an, was the sixth son of Emperor Shenwu and the full younger brother of Emperor Wenxuan.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao Yan, styled Yan'an, was the sixth son of Emperor Shenwu and the younger brother of Emperor Wenxuan by the same mother.

units.zh: 幼而英特，早有大成之量，武明皇太后早所愛重。
units.en: Even as a boy he was remarkable, showing early promise of greatness, and Empress Dowager Wuming had cherished him from the start.
units.literal: From childhood he was outstanding; early on he showed the measure of great accomplishment, and Empress Dowager Wuming had loved and esteemed him from the first.

units.zh: 魏元象元年，封常山郡公。
units.en: In the first year of the Yuanxiang era of Wei, he was made Duke of Changshan Commandery.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang of Wei, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan Commandery.

units.zh: 及文襄執政，遣中書侍郎李同軌就霸府為諸弟師。
units.en: Once Wenxiang took charge of the government, he dispatched Li Tonggui, Gentleman of the Secretariat, to the Overlord's residence to instruct his younger brothers.
units.literal: When Wenxiang came to hold power, he sent Secretariat Gentleman Li Tonggui to the Overlord's residence to serve as tutor to the younger brothers.

units.zh: 帝所覽文籍，源其指歸而不好辭彩。
units.en: In whatever he read, he sought the root meaning and cared nothing for fine phrasing.
units.literal: In the texts the Emperor read, he traced them to their underlying intent and did not care for ornamental language.

units.zh: 每歎云：「雖盟津之師，左驂震而不衄。」
units.en: He often sighed and said, "Even when the army stood at Mengjin and the left outer horse shied, they did not break and flee."
units.literal: He would often sigh and say: "Even at the army at Mengjin, though the left outer horse was startled, they did not retreat in defeat."

units.zh: 以為能。
units.en: That, he thought, was real courage.
units.literal: He regarded this as true ability.

units.zh: 遂篤志讀《漢書》，至《李陵傳》，恒壯其所為焉。
units.en: He then applied himself to the Book of Han; when he came to the biography of Li Ling, he always took fierce pride in Li Ling's conduct.
units.literal: Thereupon he devoted himself to reading the Book of Han, and when he reached the "Biography of Li Ling," he always admired what Li Ling had done.

units.zh: 聰敏過人，所與遊處，一知其家諱，終身未嘗誤犯。
units.en: Quick beyond ordinary men, he learned the taboo names of everyone he kept company with and never once, in all his life, gave accidental offense.
units.literal: His intelligence surpassed others'; those with whom he associated—he would at once learn their family taboo names, and throughout his life he never once mistakenly violated them.

units.zh: 同軌病卒，又命開府長流參軍刁柔代之，性嚴褊，不適誘訓之宜，中被遣出。
units.en: After Tonggui died of illness, Diao Rou, a senior staff officer in the chief's office, was appointed in his place—but Diao was harsh and rigid, ill suited to teaching, and before long was dismissed.
units.literal: When Tonggui died of illness, he again ordered Diao Rou, Staff Supervisor of the Chief's Office, to replace him; Diao's nature was stern and narrow, unsuited to guidance and instruction, and midway through he was dismissed and sent away.

units.zh: 帝送出閤，慘然斂容，淚數行下，左右莫不歔欷。
units.en: The prince walked him out through the gate, his face drawn and still, tears running freely; everyone around him wept.
units.literal: The Emperor escorted him out through the gate, his face grave and composed, tears streaming down in several courses; those at his side all sobbed and sighed.

units.zh: 其敬業重舊也如此。
units.en: Such was his devotion to his teachers and his loyalty to old ties.
units.literal: In his respect for his calling and esteem for old associates, he was like this.

units.zh: 天保初，進爵為王。
units.en: At the opening of the Tianbao era, he was raised to princely rank.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, his rank was advanced to prince.

units.zh: 五年，除幷省尚書令。
units.en: In the fifth year he was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat for the combined provinces.
units.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Chief Minister of the Secretariat of the Joint Provinces.

units.zh: 帝善斷割，長於文理，省內畏服。
units.en: He was sharp in judgment and strong in letters and law, and the whole Secretariat stood in awe of him.
units.literal: The Emperor was skilled at decisive judgment and excelled in literary and administrative matters; those within the Secretariat feared and submitted to him.

units.zh: 七年，從文宣還鄴。
units.en: In the seventh year he returned to Ye with Emperor Wenxuan.
units.literal: In the seventh year, he followed Wenxuan back to Ye.

units.zh: 文宣以尚書奏事，多有異同，令帝與朝臣先論定得失，然後敷奏。
units.en: Because memorials from the Secretariat often conflicted, Emperor Wenxuan had the prince and the ministers debate each matter's merits first, and only then bring the decision forward.
units.literal: Because the Secretariat's reports on affairs often contained disagreements, Wenxuan ordered the Emperor and the court officials first to discuss and settle what was right and wrong, and only then to present them formally.

units.zh: 帝長於政術，剖斷咸盡其理，文宣歎重之。
units.en: The prince had a gift for statecraft; every ruling he handed down went to the heart of the matter, and Emperor Wenxuan marveled at him.
units.literal: The Emperor excelled in the art of governance; his analyses and judgments all exhaustively addressed the principles involved, and Wenxuan sighed in admiration and held him in high esteem.

units.zh: 八年，轉司空、錄尚書事。
units.en: In the eighth year he was made Minister of Works and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred to Minister of Works and made Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 九年，除大司馬，仍錄尚書。
units.en: In the ninth year he was made Grand Marshal while retaining his post as Recorder of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the ninth year, he was appointed Grand Marshal, while still serving as Recorder of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 時文宣溺於遊宴，帝憂憤表於神色。
units.en: By then Emperor Wenxuan was lost to feasting and pleasure, and the prince's distress and anger showed in his every look.
units.literal: At that time Wenxuan was drowning himself in touring and banqueting; the Emperor's worry and indignation showed plainly in his face.

units.zh: 文宣覺之，謂帝曰：「但令汝在，我何為不縱樂？」
units.en: Emperor Wenxuan noticed and said to him, "With you here, why should I not enjoy myself?"
units.literal: Wenxuan noticed it and said to the Emperor: "As long as you are here, why should I not indulge in pleasure?"

units.zh: 帝唯啼泣拜伏，竟無所言。
units.en: The prince could only weep and bow to the ground; in the end he said not a word.
units.literal: The Emperor only wept and prostrated himself, and in the end said nothing.

units.zh: 文宣亦大悲，抵杯於地曰：「汝以此嫌我，自今敢進酒者，斬之！」
units.en: Emperor Wenxuan was stricken too. He smashed his cup on the floor and cried, "So this is how you see me! From today on, whoever dares set wine before me shall be executed!"
units.literal: Wenxuan also became deeply grieved, dashed his cup to the ground, and said: "You resent me for this—from today, anyone who dares bring wine forward shall be executed!"

units.zh: 因取所御杯盡皆壞棄。
units.en: Then he took every cup at hand and smashed them all.
units.literal: Thereupon he took all the cups he had been using and destroyed and discarded them.

units.zh: 後益沉湎，或入諸貴賤家角力批拉，不限貴賤。
units.en: After that he only sank deeper into drink. Sometimes he would walk into any house, high or low, and wrestle and brawl without distinction of rank.
units.literal: Afterwards he sank deeper into drinking; sometimes he would enter the homes of nobles and commoners alike to wrestle and grapple, with no restriction as to high or low rank.

units.zh: 唯常山王至，內外肅然。
units.en: Only when the Prince of Changshan appeared did the palace fall silent and straighten itself.
units.literal: Only when the Prince of Changshan arrived would inside and outside become solemn and awestruck.

units.zh: 帝又密撰事條，將諫，其友王晞以為不可。
units.en: The prince secretly drew up a list of grievances and prepared to remonstrate, but his friend Wang Xi urged him not to.
units.literal: The Emperor also secretly drafted a list of matters and was about to remonstrate; his friend Wang Xi thought it inadvisable.

units.zh: 帝不從，因間極言，遂逢大怒。
units.en: He would not listen. Seizing a moment alone with Emperor Wenxuan, he spoke with all his force—and provoked a terrible rage.
units.literal: The Emperor would not heed him; taking advantage of an opportune moment he spoke out to the fullest, and thereby encountered great wrath.

units.zh: 順成后本魏朝宗室，文宣欲帝離之，陰為帝廣求淑媛，望移其寵。
units.en: Empress Shuncheng came from the Wei imperial clan. Emperor Wenxuan wanted the prince to turn from her and secretly searched out worthy beauties for him, hoping to draw his heart elsewhere.
units.literal: Empress Shuncheng was originally of the imperial clan of Wei; Wenxuan wanted the Emperor to distance himself from her, and secretly sought fine ladies widely for the Emperor, hoping to shift his favor.

units.zh: 帝雖承旨有納，而情義彌重。
units.en: The prince obeyed and took some of them in, but his devotion to the empress only grew deeper.
units.literal: Though the Emperor followed the order and accepted some, his affection and attachment grew only stronger.

units.zh: 帝性頗嚴，尚書郎中剖斷有失，輒加捶楚，令史姦慝，便即考竟。
units.en: He could be severe. When a Secretariat gentleman erred in judgment, he had him beaten at once; when a clerk proved corrupt, he had him interrogated to the finish.
units.literal: The Emperor's nature was quite stern; when Secretariat Gentlemen made errors in judgment, he would immediately add beating with the whip; when clerks were deceitful and wicked, he would immediately investigate them to the end.

units.zh: 文宣乃立帝於前，以刀環擬脅召被帝罰者，臨以白刃，求帝之短，咸無所陳，方見解釋。
units.en: Emperor Wenxuan made the prince stand before him, brandishing the ring of his sword as a threat. He called in those the prince had punished, put bare blades to their throats, and demanded his faults—but none had any charge to bring, and only then was the prince released.
units.literal: Wenxuan then placed the Emperor before him, using the ring of a sword as if to threaten; summoning those whom the Emperor had punished, he confronted them with naked blades and sought the Emperor's faults—but all had nothing to report, and only then was the Emperor released and pardoned.

units.zh: 自是不許笞箠郎中。
units.en: After that he was forbidden to flog the Secretariat gentlemen.
units.literal: From then on he was not permitted to flog and beat the Gentlemen of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 後賜帝魏時宮人，醒而忘之，謂帝擅取，遂以刀環亂築，因此致困。
units.en: Later Emperor Wenxuan gave the prince palace women left from Wei times. When he sobered, he forgot the gift, accused the prince of taking them without leave, and beat him savagely with the sword ring until the prince collapsed from his injuries.
units.literal: Later Wenxuan bestowed palace women from Wei times upon the Emperor; when he sobered up he forgot about it, thought the Emperor had taken them without permission, and thereupon beat him randomly with the sword ring, causing the Emperor to fall gravely ill as a result.

units.zh: 皇太后日夜啼泣，文宣不知所為。
units.en: The Empress Dowager wept day and night, and Emperor Wenxuan did not know what to do.
units.literal: The Empress Dowager wept day and night; Wenxuan did not know what to do.

units.zh: 先是禁友王晞，乃捨之，令侍帝。
units.en: Wang Xi, his friend, had earlier been placed under restriction; now Emperor Wenxuan freed him and set him to wait on the prince.
units.literal: Earlier Wang Xi, his friend, had been confined; now he released him and ordered him to attend the Emperor.

units.zh: 帝月餘漸瘳，不敢復諫。
units.en: After a month and more the prince slowly mended, but he never dared remonstrate again.
units.literal: After more than a month the Emperor gradually recovered, but dared not remonstrate again.

units.zh: 及文宣崩，帝居禁中護喪事，幼主即位，乃即朝班。
units.en: When Emperor Wenxuan died, Xiaozhao remained in the palace to oversee the funeral. Once the young ruler took the throne, he entered the court ranks.
units.literal: When Wenxuan died, the emperor remained inside the palace to oversee the funeral arrangements; after the young ruler ascended the throne, he then took his place in the court ranks.

units.zh: 除太傅、錄尚書，朝政皆決於帝。
units.en: He was appointed grand tutor and recorder of the Masters of Writing, and all court affairs were decided by him.
units.literal: He was appointed Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and all court government was decided by the emperor.

units.zh: 月餘，乃居藩邸，自是詔勑多不關帝。
units.en: After a little over a month he withdrew to his princely residence, and from then on many edicts no longer passed through him.
units.literal: After more than a month he went to live in his princely residence, and from then on edicts and commands often did not involve the emperor.

units.zh: 客或言於帝曰：「鷙烏舍巢，必有探卵之患，今日之地，何宜屢出。」
units.en: One guest warned him, "When a bird of prey leaves the nest, someone is bound to reach for its eggs. In your present position, you should not be going out so often."
units.literal: A guest once said to the emperor, "When a fierce bird leaves its nest, there is sure to be the danger of someone probing its eggs; in your present position, you should not go out repeatedly."

units.zh: 乾明元年，從廢帝赴鄴，居於領軍府。
units.en: In Qianming 1 he accompanied Emperor Fei to Ye and resided at the headquarters of the Commanding General.
units.literal: In the first year of Qianming, he followed Emperor Fei to Ye and lived at the headquarters of the Commanding General.

units.zh: 時楊愔、燕子獻、可朱渾天和、宋欽道、鄭子默等以帝威望旣重，內懼權逼，請以帝為太師、司州牧、錄尚書事；
units.en: At the time Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Kezhuhun Tianhe, Song Qindao, Zheng Zimo, and the others saw how great his prestige had become and secretly feared the pressure of his authority. They asked that he be made grand preceptor, governor of Sizhou, and recorder of the Masters of Writing;
units.literal: At the time Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Kezhuhun Tianhe, Song Qindao, Zheng Zimo, and others, because the emperor’s prestige had become weighty and they inwardly feared the pressure of his power, requested that he be made Grand Preceptor, governor of Sizhou, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing;

units.zh: 長廣王湛為大司馬、錄幷省尚書事，解京畿大都督。
units.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang was appointed grand marshal and recorder of the Masters of Writing in the Bingzhou administration, and was relieved of the capital-region command.
units.literal: Prince Zhan of Changguang was made Grand Marshal and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing in Bing Province, and was relieved as metropolitan commander of the capital region.

units.zh: 帝時以尊親而見猜斥，乃與長廣王期獵，謀之於野。
units.en: Because his rank and kinship made him suspect, Xiaozhao was being pushed aside. He therefore arranged a hunt with Prince Zhan of Changguang and plotted with him in the field.
units.literal: The emperor at that time, because he was an honored kinsman, was regarded with suspicion and pushed aside; he therefore arranged to hunt with the Prince of Changguang and plotted with him in the countryside.

units.zh: 三月甲戌，帝初上省，旦發領軍府，大風暴起，壞所御車幔，帝甚惡之。
units.en: On the jiaxu day of the third month, the prince went to the Secretariat for the first time. At dawn he left the Commander-in-Chief's headquarters; a sudden gale tore the curtains of his carriage, and he took it as a dire omen.
units.literal: On the jiaxu day of the third month, the Emperor for the first time went to the Secretariat; at dawn he set out from the Commander-in-Chief's office; a violent windstorm arose and destroyed the curtains of his carriage—the Emperor regarded it as highly ominous.

units.zh: 及至省，朝士咸集。
units.en: By the time he arrived, the court officials had all gathered.
units.literal: When he reached the Secretariat, all the court officials had assembled.

units.zh: 坐定，酒數行，執尚書令楊愔、右僕射燕子獻、領軍可朱渾天和、侍中宋欽道等於坐。
units.en: They had barely settled in and taken a few cups when he seized Chief Minister Yang Yin, Right Vice Director Yanzi Xian, Commander-in-Chief Kezhuhun Tianhe, Palace Attendant Song Qindao, and the rest where they sat.
units.literal: Once seated, after a few rounds of wine, he seized Chief Minister Yang Yin, Right Deputy Director Yanzi Xian, Commander-in-Chief Kezhuhun Tianhe, Palace Attendant Song Qindao, and others at the banquet.

units.zh: 帝戎服與平原王段韶、平秦王高歸彥、領軍劉洪徽入自雲龍門，於中書省前遇散騎常侍鄭子默，又執之，同斬於御府之內。
units.en: In armor, with Prince Duan Shao of Pingyuan, Prince Gao Guiyan of Pingqin, and Commander-in-Chief Liu Honghui, he entered through the Cloud Dragon Gate. Before the Secretariat he met Regular Attendant Zheng Zimo, seized him too, and had them all beheaded inside the Imperial Treasury.
units.literal: The Emperor, in military garb, together with Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao, Prince of Pingqin Gao Guiyan, and Commander-in-Chief Liu Honghui, entered through the Cloud Dragon Gate; before the Secretariat they encountered Regular Attendant Zheng Zimo, seized him as well, and beheaded them all together inside the Imperial Treasury.

units.zh: 帝至東閤門，都督成休甯抽刃呵帝。
units.en: At the Eastern Pavilion Gate, the commander Cheng Xiuning drew his sword and shouted at the prince.
units.literal: The Emperor reached the Eastern Pavilion Gate; the Commander Cheng Xiuning drew his blade and shouted at the Emperor.

units.zh: 帝令高歸彥喻之，休甯厲聲大呼不從。
units.en: The prince sent Gao Guiyan to reason with him, but Xiuning roared his refusal.
units.literal: The Emperor ordered Gao Guiyan to explain to him; Xiuning shouted loudly and would not obey.

units.zh: 歸彥旣為領軍，素為兵士所服，悉皆弛仗，休寧歎息而罷。
units.en: Gao Guiyan, now Commander-in-Chief, was a man the troops had long trusted. At his word they lowered their arms, and Xiuning sighed and stood down.
units.literal: Gao Guiyan, having become Commander-in-Chief, was long respected by the soldiers; all laid down their weapons, and Xiuning sighed and desisted.

units.zh: 帝入至昭陽殿，幼主、太皇太后、皇太后並出臨御坐。
units.en: The prince entered Zhaoyang Hall. The young emperor, the Grand Empress Dowager, and the Empress Dowager all came out to the throne.
units.literal: The Emperor entered to Zhaoyang Hall; the young emperor, the Grand Empress Dowager, and the Empress Dowager all came out to the imperial throne.

units.zh: 帝奏愔等罪，求伏專擅之辜。
units.en: He laid out the crimes of Yang Yin and his fellows and asked to bear the penalty for acting on his own authority.
units.literal: The Emperor reported the crimes of Yin and the others, and requested to accept guilt for having acted with sole authority.

units.zh: 時庭中及兩廊下衛士二千餘人皆被甲待詔，武衛娥永樂武力絕綸，又被文宣重遇，撫刃思效。
units.en: More than two thousand guards in the courtyard and along both wings of the hall stood armored, awaiting command. E Yongle of the Military Guard was a fighter without equal, and Emperor Wenxuan had greatly favored him; he gripped his blade, ready to give his life.
units.literal: At that time more than two thousand guards in the courtyard and beneath both corridor wings all donned armor awaiting orders; military guard E Yongle's martial prowess was unmatched, and he had also been greatly favored by Wenxuan; he grasped his blade, thinking to devote himself.

units.zh: 廢帝性吃訥，兼倉卒不知所言。
units.en: Emperor Fei, now deposed, was slow of tongue and halting in speech; caught in the sudden crisis, he did not know what to say.
units.literal: Deposed Emperor Fei's nature was stuttering and slow of speech; moreover, in the sudden emergency he did not know what to say.

units.zh: 太皇太后又為皇后誓，言帝無異志，唯去逼而已。
units.en: The Grand Empress Dowager also swore on the empress's behalf that the prince harbored no treasonous design and had acted only to remove those who had been coercing the throne.
units.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager also swore on behalf of the empress, saying the Emperor had no rebellious intent and had only removed those who were pressuring him.

units.zh: 高歸彥勑勞衛士解嚴，永樂乃內刀而泣。
units.en: Gao Guiyan ordered the guards to stand down and thanked them for their service; E Yongle then sheathed his blade and wept.
units.literal: Gao Guiyan ordered and comforted the guards to lift martial law; Yongle then sheathed his blade and wept.

units.zh: 帝乃令歸彥引侍衛之士向華林園，以京畿軍入守門閤，斬娥永樂於園。
units.en: The prince then ordered Gao Guiyan to lead the palace guards to Hualin Garden, posted the capital garrison at the palace gates, and executed E Yongle there.
units.literal: The Emperor then ordered Guiyan to lead the palace guards toward Hualin Garden, had the capital garrison troops enter to hold the gate towers, and executed E Yongle in the garden.

units.zh: 詔以帝為大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，相府佐史進位一等。
units.en: An edict appointed him Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat, and all staff of the chancellery were promoted one rank.
units.literal: An edict appointed the Emperor Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat; assistants and clerks of the chancellery were promoted one rank.

units.zh: 帝尋如晉陽，有詔軍國大政咸諮決焉。
units.en: The prince soon proceeded to Jinyang, where an edict declared that all major civil and military affairs were to be submitted to him for final decision.
units.literal: The Emperor soon went to Jinyang; an edict stated that all major state and military affairs were to be referred to him for decision.

units.zh: 帝旣當大位，知無不為，擇其令典，考綜名實，廢帝恭己以聽政。
units.en: Once he held real power, he left nothing undone—choosing the best laws, matching appointments to actual merit—while the deposed emperor modestly yielded the throne and listened to his governance.
units.literal: Once the Emperor had assumed supreme power, there was nothing he did not undertake; he selected the finest statutes, examined names against realities, and the deposed emperor humbly yielded to listen to governance.

units.zh: 太皇太后尋下令廢少主，命帝統大業。
units.en: The Grand Empress Dowager soon issued an order deposing the young emperor and commanding him to take up the imperial succession.
units.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager soon issued an order deposing the young ruler and commanding the Emperor to inherit the great enterprise.

units.zh: 皇建元年八月壬午，皇帝即位於晉陽宣德殿，大赦，改乾明元年為皇建。
units.en: On the renwu day of the eighth month of the first year of Huangjian, the emperor ascended the throne in the Xuande Hall at Jinyang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name from Qianming to Huangjian.
units.literal: On the renwu day of the eighth month of Huangjian year 1, the emperor ascended the throne in the Xuande Hall at Jinyang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name from Qianming year 1 to Huangjian.

units.zh: 詔奉太皇太后還稱皇太后，皇太后稱文宣皇后，宮曰昭信。
units.en: An edict restored the Grand Empress Dowager to the title of Empress Dowager, gave the former empress dowager the title Empress Wenxuan, and named her residence Zhaoxin Palace.
units.literal: An edict restored the Grand Empress Dowager to the title of Empress Dowager; the Empress Dowager was given the title Empress Wenxuan, and her palace was named Zhaoxin.

units.zh: 乙酉，詔自太祖創業已來，諸有佐命功臣子孫絕滅，國統不傳者，有司搜訪近親，以名聞，當量為立後；
units.en: On the yiyou day, an edict declared that since the Founding Emperor's rise to power, wherever the descendants of founding ministers had died out and their lines of succession were broken, officials should search for close relatives, report their names, and appoint successors as appropriate.
units.literal: On the yiyou day, an edict stated that from the time the Founding Emperor established the enterprise, wherever meritorious founding ministers' descendants had died out and the line of succession was broken, the responsible offices should search out close relatives, report their names, and appoint successors as appropriate.

units.zh: 諸郡國老人各授版職，賜黃帽鳩杖。
units.en: Elderly men throughout the commanderies and principalities were granted honorary appointments and presented with yellow caps and dove staffs.
units.literal: Elderly persons in all commanderies and principalities were granted honorary rank plaques and given yellow caps and dove staffs.

units.zh: 又詔謇正之士並聽進見陳事；
units.en: Another edict permitted upright and outspoken men to come forward and address the throne directly.
units.literal: Another edict also allowed upright and forthright men to come forward and present matters to the throne.

units.zh: 軍人戰亡死王事者，以時申聞，當加榮贈；
units.en: Soldiers who fell in battle or died in the ruler's service were to be reported promptly and granted posthumous honors.
units.literal: Soldiers who died in battle or in service to the ruler were to be reported in timely fashion and honored with posthumous awards.

units.zh: 督將、朝士名望素高，位歷通顯，天保以來未蒙追贈者，亦皆錄奏；
units.en: Military governors and court officials of high standing who had held prominent posts but had not received posthumous honors since the Tianbao era were also to be recorded and memorialized.
units.literal: Military governors and court officials of longstanding high reputation who had held prominent posts but since Tianbao had not received posthumous honors—all these were also to be recorded and memorialized.

units.zh: 又以廷尉、中丞，執法所在，繩違按罪，不得舞文弄法；
units.en: It further ordered the Court of Judicial Review and the Censorate, as the organs charged with enforcing the law, to investigate violations and assign guilt strictly according to statute, without twisting the law for their own purposes.
units.literal: It further ordered that the Court of Judicial Review and the Censorate, as the organs of law enforcement, must investigate violations and assign guilt according to the law, and must not distort the law through verbal manipulation.

units.zh: 其官奴婢年六十已上免為庶人。
units.en: Official slaves aged sixty or older were freed and made commoners.
units.literal: Official slave servants aged sixty and above were freed to become commoners.

units.zh: 戊子，以太傅、長廣王湛為右丞相，以太尉、平陽王淹為太傅，以尚書令、彭城王浟為大司馬。
units.en: On wuzi, Prince Zhan of Changguang, then grand tutor, became right chancellor; Prince Yan of Pingyang, then grand commandant, became grand tutor; and Prince You of Pengcheng, director of the Masters of Writing, became grand marshal.
units.literal: On wuzi, the Grand Tutor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, was appointed Right Chancellor; the Grand Commandant, Prince Yan of Pingyang, was appointed Grand Tutor; and the Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince You of Pengcheng, was appointed Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 壬辰，詔分遣大使巡省四方，觀察風俗，問人疾苦，考求得失，搜訪賢良。
units.en: On the renchen day, an edict ordered envoys to be sent throughout the realm to inspect local conditions, inquire into the people's hardships, assess what had succeeded or failed, and seek out worthy and able men.
units.literal: On the renchen day, an edict ordered envoys to be dispatched in all directions to tour and inspect the realm, observe local customs, inquire into the people's hardships, examine gains and losses, and search out the worthy and able.

units.zh: 甲午，詔曰：「昔武王克殷，先封兩代，漢、魏、二晉，無廢茲典。
units.en: On the jiawu day, an edict stated: "When King Wu of Zhou conquered the Shang, he first enfeoffed descendants of the two preceding dynasties. The Han, Wei, and two Jin dynasties likewise never abandoned this precedent.
units.literal: On the jiawu day, an edict said: "In antiquity, when King Wu conquered Yin, he first enfeoffed the two former dynasties; Han, Wei, and the two Jin dynasties did not abandon this precedent.

units.zh: 及元氏統歷，不率舊章。
units.en: But when the Northern Wei held power, they ceased to follow the old rites.
units.literal: When the Yuan clan held the succession, they did not follow the old statutes.

units.zh: 朕纂承大業，思弘古典，但二王三恪，舊說不同，可議定是非，列名條奏。
units.en: We have inherited the imperial enterprise and wish to restore the ancient practice, but scholars disagree on the rites for enfeoffing descendants of prior dynasties; let the matter be debated, the correct view determined, and the names submitted in memorial.
units.literal: We have inherited the great enterprise and wish to restore the ancient model, but the old accounts differ on the two kings and three classes of former dynasties; the right and wrong should be debated and determined, and the names listed in a memorial.

units.zh: 其禮義體式亦仰議之。」
units.en: The ritual forms and ceremonial standards should likewise be submitted for deliberation."
units.literal: The ritual forms and ceremonial standards should also be submitted for deliberation."

units.zh: 又詔國子寺可備立官屬，依舊置生，請習經典，歲時考試。
units.en: Another edict ordered the Directorate of the National University to restore its full staff, enroll students as before, have them study the classics, and hold seasonal examinations.
units.literal: Another edict stated that the Directorate of the National University should fully establish its official staff, enroll students as before, have them study the classics, and hold examinations at the proper seasons.

units.zh: 其文襄帝所運石經，宜即施列於學館。
units.en: The stone classics commissioned by Emperor Wenxiang should immediately be set up and displayed in the academy.
units.literal: The stone classics transported by Emperor Wenxiang should immediately be set up and displayed in the academy halls.

units.zh: 外州大學亦仰典司勤加督課。
units.en: The provincial universities should likewise be diligently supervised and examined by the responsible offices.
units.literal: The provincial universities should also be diligently supervised and examined by the responsible offices.

units.zh: 丙申，詔九州勳人有重封者，聽分授子弟，以廣骨肉之恩。
units.en: On the bingshen day, an edict declared that meritorious men of the nine provinces who held multiple enfeoffments might divide and grant them to sons and younger brothers, so as to extend the bonds of kinship.
units.literal: On the bingshen day, an edict stated that meritorious men of the nine provinces who held double enfeoffments might divide and grant them to their sons and younger brothers, to broaden the ties of kinship.

units.zh: 九月壬申，詔議定三祖樂。
units.en: On the renshen day of the ninth month, an edict ordered deliberation on the ritual music for the three ancestral temples.
units.literal: On the renshen day of the ninth month, an edict ordered deliberation on the music for the three ancestral temples.

units.zh: 冬十一月辛亥，立妃元氏為皇后，世子百年為皇太子。
units.en: On the xinhai day of the eleventh month, Consort Yuan was installed as empress and the heir apparent Gao Bainian as crown prince.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on the xinhai day, Consort Yuan was installed as empress and the heir apparent Bainian as crown prince.

units.zh: 賜天下為父後者爵一級。
units.en: All men throughout the realm who were heirs to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.
units.literal: All who served as heirs to their fathers throughout the realm were granted one rank of nobility.

units.zh: 癸丑，有司奏太祖獻武皇帝廟宜奏《武德》之樂，舞《昭烈》之舞；
units.en: On the guichou day, officials memorialized that the temple of the Founding Emperor, Emperor Xianwu, should use the hymn "Martial Virtue" and the dance "Illustrious Fierceness."
units.literal: On the guichou day, the responsible offices memorialized that the temple of the Founding Emperor, Emperor Xianwu, should use the music "Wude" and the dance "Zhaolie."

units.zh: 世宗文襄皇帝廟宜奏《文德》之樂，舞《宣政》之舞；
units.en: The temple of Emperor Wenxiang should use the hymn "Civil Virtue" and the dance "Proclaiming Governance."
units.literal: The temple of Emperor Wenxiang should use the music "Wende" and the dance "Xuanzheng."

units.zh: 顯祖文宣皇帝廟宜奏《文正》之樂，舞《光大》之舞。
units.en: The temple of Emperor Wenxuan should use the hymn "Correct Civil Virtue" and the dance "Great Radiance."
units.literal: The temple of Emperor Wenxuan should use the music "Wenzheng" and the dance "Guangda."

units.zh: 詔曰可。
units.en: The edict approved the proposal.
units.literal: An edict said it was approved.

units.zh: 庚申，詔以故太師尉景、故太師竇泰、故太師太原王婁昭、故太宰章武王厙狄幹、故太尉段榮、故太師万俟普、故司徒蔡儁、故太師高乾、故司徒莫多婁貸文、故太保劉貴、故太保封祖裔、故廣州刺史王懷十二人配饗太祖廟庭，故太師清河王岳、故太宰安德王韓軌、故太宰扶風王可朱渾道元、故太師高昂、故大司馬劉豐、故太師万俟受洛干、故太尉慕容紹宗七人配饗世宗廟庭，故太尉河東王潘相樂、故司空薛脩義、故太傅破六韓常三人配饗顯祖廟庭。
units.en: On the gengshen day, an edict ordered twelve deceased ministers to receive associated sacrifice in the Founding Emperor's temple, including Wei Jing, Dou Tai, Lou Zhao, She Digan, Duan Rong, Wan Sipo, Cai Jun, Gao Gan, Moduo Lou Daiwen, Liu Gui, Feng Zuyi, and Wang Huai; seven others in Emperor Wenxiang's temple, including Princes Yue, Han Gui, and Kezhuhun Daoyuan, Liu Feng, Wan Sipo Shouluogan, and Murong Shaozong; and three more in Emperor Wenxuan's temple—Pan Xiangle, Xue Xiuyi, and Poliuhan Chang.
units.literal: On the gengshen day, an edict ordered that the late Grand Preceptor Wei Jing, Grand Preceptor Dou Tai, Grand Preceptor Prince of Taiyuan Lou Zhao, Grand Minister Prince of Zhangwu She Digan, Grand Commander Duan Rong, Grand Preceptor Wan Sipo, Minister of Education Cai Jun, Grand Preceptor Gao Gan, Minister of Education Moduo Lou Daiwen, Grand Guardian Liu Gui, Grand Guardian Feng Zuyi, and Inspector of Guang Province Wang Huai—twelve men in all—be given associated sacrifice in the Founding Emperor's temple court; that Grand Preceptor Prince of Qinghe Yue, Grand Minister Prince of Ande Han Gui, Grand Minister Prince of Fufeng Kezhuhun Daoyuan, Grand Preceptor Gao Ao, Grand Marshal Liu Feng, Grand Preceptor Wan Sipo Shouluogan, and Grand Commander Murong Shaozong—seven men—be given associated sacrifice in Emperor Wenxiang's temple court; and that Grand Commander Prince of Hedong Pan Xiangle, Minister of Works Xue Xiuyi, and Grand Tutor Poliuhan Chang—three men—be given associated sacrifice in Emperor Wenxuan's temple court.

units.zh: 是月，帝親戎北討庫莫奚，出長城，虜奔遁，分兵致討，大獲牛馬，括總入晉陽宮。
units.en: That month the emperor personally led a campaign north against the Kumo Xi. He passed beyond the Great Wall; the enemy fled in rout; he sent columns in pursuit and captured large herds of cattle and horses, which were tallied and brought into Jinyang Palace.
units.literal: That month, the emperor personally took the field and marched north to attack the Kumo Xi; he passed beyond the Great Wall, the enemy fled in rout, he sent troops in separate columns to pursue them, captured large numbers of cattle and horses, and tallied the whole and brought it into Jinyang Palace.

units.zh: 十二月丙午，車駕至晉陽。
units.en: On the bingwu day of the twelfth month, the emperor arrived at Jinyang.
units.literal: On the bingwu day of the twelfth month, the imperial carriage arrived at Jinyang.

units.zh: 二年春正月辛亥，祀圓丘。
units.en: On the xinhai day of the first month of the second year, he sacrificed at the Altar of Heaven.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of year 2, on the xinhai day, he sacrificed at the Round Altar.

units.zh: 壬子，禘於太廟。
units.en: On the renzi day, he performed the di sacrifice at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
units.literal: On the renzi day, he performed the di sacrifice at the Grand Ancestral Temple.

units.zh: 癸丑，詔降罪人各有差。
units.en: On the guichou day, an edict commuted the sentences of criminals, each according to the circumstances of his case.
units.literal: On the guichou day, an edict reduced the sentences of criminals, each according to his case.

units.zh: 二月丁丑，詔內外執事之官從五品已上及三府主簿錄事參軍、諸王文學、侍御史、廷尉三官、尚書郎中、中書舍人，每二年之內各舉一人。
units.en: On the dingchou day of the second month, an edict ordered that every two years each official of fifth rank or above in the central and provincial governments, along with chief clerks of the Three Offices, literary instructors to the princes, attendant censors, judicial review officials, ministry directors, and secretariat drafters, should each recommend one candidate.
units.literal: On the dingchou day of the second month, an edict ordered that within every two years, each official from fifth rank and above in inner and outer service, as well as chief clerks and recording secretaries of the Three Offices, literary instructors of the princes, attendant censors, the three officials of the Court of Judicial Review, directors of the Ministries, and secretaries of the Secretariat, should each recommend one man.

units.zh: 冬十月丙子，以尚書令、彭城王浟為太保，長樂王尉粲為太尉。
units.en: On the bingzi day of the tenth month, Director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Pengcheng Gao You was made Grand Guardian, and Prince of Changle Wei Can was made Grand Commander.
units.literal: On the bingzi day of the tenth month of winter, Director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Pengcheng Gao You was appointed Grand Guardian, and Prince of Changle Wei Can was appointed Grand Commander.

units.zh: 己酉，野雉棲于前殿之庭。
units.en: On the jiyou day, wild pheasants roosted in the courtyard of the front hall.
units.literal: On the jiyou day, wild pheasants roosted in the court of the front hall.

units.zh: 十一月甲辰，詔曰：「朕嬰此暴疾，奄忽無逮。
units.en: In the eleventh month, on jiachen, an edict declared, "I have been struck by a sudden grave illness and can no longer attend to affairs.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiachen, an edict said: "I have been stricken by this violent illness and suddenly can no longer reach affairs.

units.zh: 今嗣子沖眇，未閑政術，社稷業重，理歸上德。
units.en: The heir is young and slight, not yet versed in statecraft. The charge of the dynasty is heavy, and by rights it should pass to one of highest virtue.
units.literal: Now the heir is young and slight, not yet practiced in the arts of government; the work of the altars of soil and grain is weighty, and by principle it returns to one of highest virtue.

units.zh: 右丞相、長廣王湛研機測化，體道居宗，人雄之望，海內瞻仰，同胞共氣，家國所憑，可遣尚書左僕射、趙郡王叡喻旨，征王統茲大寶。
units.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang, right chancellor, understands hidden workings and change, embodies the Way, and stands foremost among the clan. The whole realm looks to him as a hero among men. Born of the same mother and sharing the same breath, he is the support of house and state. Send Prince Rui of Zhaojun, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, to convey my intent and summon him to take charge of the throne.
units.literal: The Right Chancellor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, studies subtle workings and fathoms transformation, embodies the Way and stands within the clan; as a hero among men, he is looked up to within the seas. Of the same womb and shared breath, he is one on whom house and state rely. The Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Rui of Zhaojun, may be sent to explain the intent and summon the prince to govern this great treasure.

units.zh: 其喪紀之禮一同漢文，三十六日悉從公除，山陵施用，務從儉約。」
units.en: As for mourning rites, follow entirely the precedent of Emperor Wen of Han. After thirty-six days all mourning shall be removed according to public rule, and the mausoleum expenses must be kept frugal."
units.literal: As for the rites of mourning, let all be the same as under Emperor Wen of Han; after thirty-six days, all shall follow public removal of mourning, and the expenditures for the mountain mausoleum must follow frugality."

units.zh: 先是帝不豫而無闕聽覽，是月，崩於晉陽宮，時年二十七。
units.en: Before this the emperor had been ill, yet he had not neglected audiences or reviews of affairs. That month he died in Jinyang Palace at the age of twenty-seven.
units.literal: Before this, the emperor had been ill but had not neglected hearings and review; that month he died in Jinyang Palace, aged twenty-seven.

units.zh: 大寧元年閏十二月癸卯，梓宮還鄴，上諡曰孝昭皇帝。
units.en: In the intercalary twelfth month of Daning 1, on guimao, his coffin was returned to Ye, and he was given the posthumous title Emperor Xiaozhao.
units.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month of the first year of Daning, on guimao, the imperial coffin returned to Ye, and the posthumous title Emperor Xiaozhao was presented.

units.zh: 庚午，葬於文靖陵。
units.en: On gengwu he was buried in Wenjing Mausoleum.
units.literal: On gengwu, he was buried in Wenjing Mausoleum.

units.zh: 帝聰敏有識度，深沉能斷，不可窺測。
units.en: The emperor was quick-witted and far-sighted, deep and decisive—his inner thoughts could not be read.
units.literal: The emperor was keen and perceptive, with breadth of judgment; deep and resolute, he could not be fathomed.

units.zh: 身長八尺，腰帶十圍，儀望風表，迥然獨秀。
units.en: He stood eight feet tall, with a waist ten spans around; in bearing and presence he stood apart, towering above all others.
units.literal: He stood eight feet tall, with a waist ten spans around; in bearing and appearance he stood alone, towering above others.

units.zh: 自居臺省，留心政術，閑明簿領，吏所不逮。
units.en: From his years in the central administration he devoted himself to governance and mastered records and accounts with a clarity clerks could not match.
units.literal: From the time he held office in the central administration, he devoted himself to the art of governance and was clear and skilled in records and registers, beyond what clerks could match.

units.zh: 及正位宸居，彌所剋勵。
units.en: Once he ascended the throne, he applied himself all the more vigorously.
units.literal: Once he took the imperial throne, he applied himself all the more vigorously.

units.zh: 輕徭薄賦，勤恤人隱。
units.en: He lightened corvée labor and reduced taxes, and diligently attended to the people's hidden hardships.
units.literal: He lightened corvée labor and reduced taxes, and diligently cared for the people's hidden hardships.

units.zh: 內無私寵，外收人物，雖后父位亦特進無別。
units.en: He showed no private favoritism within the palace and gathered talented men from without; even the empress's father, for all his honors, received no special treatment beyond his nominal rank.
units.literal: Within the palace he showed no private favoritism; outside he gathered men of talent, and even the empress's father, though honored, received no special treatment beyond his nominal rank.

units.zh: 日昃臨朝，務知人之善惡，每訪問左右，冀獲直言。
units.en: He held court until the sun was low in the west, striving to discern men's strengths and failings; he constantly questioned those around him, hoping to hear frank counsel.
units.literal: He held court until the sun slanted westward, striving to know men's good and bad qualities; he constantly questioned those around him, hoping to obtain frank speech.

units.zh: 曾問舍人裴澤在外議論得失。
units.en: He once asked Attendant Gentleman Pei Ze what people were saying about his policies when he was away from court.
units.literal: He once asked the Attendant Gentleman Pei Ze what was said about gains and losses when he was abroad.

units.zh: 澤率爾對曰：「陛下聰明至公，自可遠侔古昔，而有識之士，咸言傷細，帝王之度，頗為未弘。」
units.en: Pei Ze answered without hesitation: "Your Majesty is intelligent and utterly fair and could indeed rival the sages of antiquity, but men of discernment all say you are too exacting in small matters—the magnanimity proper to an emperor is still somewhat lacking."
units.literal: Ze answered straight off: "Your Majesty is intelligent and utterly fair and could indeed rival the ancients of old, but men of discernment all say you are too exacting in small matters; the magnanimity proper to an emperor is still somewhat lacking."

units.zh: 帝笑曰：「誠如卿言。
units.en: The emperor smiled and said, "You are quite right.
units.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "It is truly as you say.

units.zh: 朕初臨萬機，慮不周悉，故致爾耳。
units.en: When I first assumed the throne, I had not yet grasped every detail of governance, and that is why this happened.
units.literal: When I first took charge of the myriad affairs of state, my concerns were not thorough and complete; that is why this came about.

units.zh: 此事安可久行，恐後又嫌疏漏。」
units.en: This cannot go on indefinitely—I am afraid you will later find me negligent again."
units.literal: How can this matter be carried on for long? I fear that afterward you will again find omissions.

units.zh: 澤因被寵遇。
units.en: Pei Ze was thereupon showered with imperial favor.
units.literal: Thereupon Pei Ze received favored treatment.

units.zh: 其樂聞過也如此。
units.en: Such was his pleasure in being told of his faults.
units.literal: His delight in hearing of his faults was like this.

units.zh: 趙郡王叡與厙狄顯安侍坐，帝曰：「須拔我同堂弟，顯安我親姑子，今序家人禮，除君臣之敬，可言我之不逮。」
units.en: Prince of Zhao Gao Rui and Kudi Xian'an were seated in attendance. The emperor said, "Xu Ba is my cousin; Xian'an is my aunt's son. Today we observe family etiquette and put aside the formalities of ruler and subject—you may tell me where I fall short."
units.literal: Prince of Zhao Rui and Kudi Xian'an were in attendance seated beside him. The Emperor said: "Xu Ba is my paternal cousin; Xian'an is the son of my paternal aunt. Today let us observe family rites and set aside the respect due between ruler and minister—you may speak of where I fall short.

units.zh: 顯安曰：「陛下多妄言。」
units.en: Xian'an said, "Your Majesty says many things that are not true."
units.literal: Xian'an said: "Your Majesty speaks many reckless words.

units.zh: 曰：「若何？」
units.en: The emperor asked, "How so?"
units.literal: He said: "How so?

units.zh: 對曰：「陛下昔見文宣以馬鞭撻人，常以為非，而今行之，非妄言耶？」
units.en: He replied, "Your Majesty once saw Emperor Wenxuan lash people with a riding crop and always condemned it; yet now you do the same—is that not saying one thing and doing another?"
units.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty once saw Emperor Wenxuan beat people with a horsewhip and always regarded it as wrong; yet now you do the same—is this not reckless speech?

units.zh: 帝握其手謝之。
units.en: The emperor took his hand and thanked him.
units.literal: The Emperor grasped his hand and apologized to him.

units.zh: 又使直言。
units.en: He again asked them to speak plainly.
units.literal: He again had them speak frankly.

units.zh: 對曰：「陛下太細，天子乃更似吏。」
units.en: They replied, "Your Majesty is too detail-minded—the Son of Heaven ends up acting more like a petty official."
units.literal: They replied: "Your Majesty is too meticulous; the Son of Heaven ends up seeming more like a clerk.

units.zh: 帝曰：「朕甚知之，然無法來久，將整之以至無為耳。」
units.en: The emperor said, "I am well aware of that, but things cannot stay this way forever. I mean to set affairs in order until governance can proceed effortlessly on its own."
units.literal: The Emperor said: "I know this very well; yet it cannot go on like this for long. I intend to put things in order so as ultimately to achieve non-action.

units.zh: 又問王晞，晞答如顯安，皆從容受納。
units.en: He then questioned Wang Xi, who answered as Xian'an had; the emperor received all their remarks with composure.
units.literal: He again asked Wang Xi; Xi answered as Xian'an had, and all were calmly accepted.

units.zh: 性至孝，太后不豫，出居南宮，帝行不正履，容色貶悴，衣不解帶，殆將四旬。
units.en: He was deeply filial. When the empress dowager fell ill and moved to the Southern Palace, the emperor walked unsteadily, his face gaunt and drawn; he slept in his clothes without removing his belt for nearly forty days.
units.literal: By nature he was extremely filial. When the Empress Dowager fell ill and moved to the Southern Palace, the Emperor did not walk with proper gait, his countenance was haggard and worn, he did not remove his belt, for nearly forty days.

units.zh: 殿去南宮五百餘步，雞鳴而去，辰時方還，來去徒行，不乘輿輦。
units.en: The palace hall was over five hundred paces from the Southern Palace. He rose at cockcrow and did not return until mid-morning, walking the whole way on foot without taking a carriage or palanquin.
units.literal: The hall was more than five hundred paces from the Southern Palace. He rose at cockcrow and returned only at the chen hour; coming and going he walked on foot and did not ride in carriage or palanquin.

units.zh: 太后所苦小增，便即寢伏閤外，食飲藥物盡皆躬親。
units.en: Whenever the empress dowager's illness worsened even slightly, he would immediately bed down outside her chamber and personally attend to all her food, drink, and medicine.
units.literal: Whenever the Empress Dowager's affliction increased even slightly, he at once lay down to sleep outside her chamber door; food, drink, and medicines he attended to entirely in person.

units.zh: 太后常心痛不自堪忍，帝立侍帷前，以爪掐手心，血流出袖。
units.en: When the empress dowager was often racked with unbearable heart pain, the emperor would stand in attendance before her curtain, digging his nails into his palms until blood ran down his sleeves.
units.literal: The Empress Dowager often suffered heart pain she could not bear. The Emperor stood attending before the curtain, digging his fingernails into his palms until blood flowed down his sleeves.

units.zh: 友愛諸弟，無君臣之隔。
units.en: He was loving toward his younger brothers, with none of the distance that normally separates ruler from subject.
units.literal: He was affectionate toward his younger brothers, with no barrier of ruler and minister between them.

units.zh: 雄斷有謀，于時國富兵強，將雪神武遺恨，意在頓駕平陽，為進取之策。
units.en: Bold and decisive, he was also a man of strategy. The realm was then rich and its armies strong, and he meant to avenge the grievances left by Emperor Shenwu, planning to establish his headquarters at Pingyang as a base for conquest.
units.literal: Bold in decision and possessed of strategy, at that time the state was rich and the army strong; he wished to avenge Emperor Shenwu's lingering resentment and intended to encamp at Pingyang as a strategy for advance.

units.zh: 遠圖不遂，惜哉！
units.en: His grand designs were never realized—what a pity!
units.literal: His distant designs were not fulfilled—alas!

units.zh: 初，帝與濟南約不相害。
units.en: At first the emperor and the Prince of Jinan had pledged not to harm each other.
units.literal: Initially the Emperor and the Prince of Jinan agreed not to harm each other.

units.zh: 及輿駕在晉陽，武成鎮鄴，望氣者云鄴城有天子氣。
units.en: When the emperor was at Jinyang and Wucheng (Gao Zhan) held Ye, geomancers declared that Ye possessed the aura of imperial destiny.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Jinyang and Wucheng was stationed at Ye, practitioners of qi-reading said Ye city had the aura of a Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 帝常恐濟南復興，乃密行鳩毒，濟南不從，乃扼而殺之。
units.en: The emperor, fearing that the Prince of Jinan might regain power, secretly sent poison; when the prince refused to take it, he was strangled to death.
units.literal: The Emperor often feared the Prince of Jinan would rise again, and so secretly administered poison; when the Prince of Jinan refused, he strangled him to death.

units.zh: 後頗愧悔。
units.en: Afterward he was deeply remorseful.
units.literal: Afterward he felt considerable remorse.

units.zh: 初苦內熱，頻進湯散。
units.en: At first he was troubled by internal fever and took medicinal broths and powders repeatedly.
units.literal: At first he suffered from internal heat and frequently took decoctions and powders.

units.zh: 時有尚書令史姓趙，於鄴見文宣從楊愔、燕子獻等西行，言相與復讐。
units.en: A clerk in the Secretariat surnamed Zhao, while at Ye, saw a vision of Emperor Wenxuan leading Yang Yin, Yan Zixian, and others westward, saying they had come to take revenge.
units.literal: At that time there was a Secretariat clerk surnamed Zhao who, at Ye, saw Wenxuan leading Yang Yin, Yan Zixian, and others heading west, saying they were coming together to take revenge.

units.zh: 帝在晉陽宮，與毛夫人亦見焉。
units.en: The emperor, in the Jinyang Palace, saw the same vision, as did Lady Mao.
units.literal: The Emperor, at Jinyang Palace, along with Lady Mao, also saw it.

units.zh: 遂漸危篤。
units.en: His illness thereupon grew steadily worse.
units.literal: Thereupon his condition gradually became critical.

units.zh: 備禳厭之事，或煮油四灑，或持炬燒逐。
units.en: Every sort of exorcism was performed—oil was boiled and splashed in all directions, or torches were carried to burn and drive spirits away.
units.literal: He prepared exorcistic and apotropaic rites: sometimes boiling oil and sprinkling it in all directions, sometimes holding torches to burn and drive away spirits.

units.zh: 諸厲方出殿梁，騎棟上，歌呼自若，了無懼容。
units.en: When evil spirits seemed to emerge from the palace beams, he climbed onto the rafters, singing and shouting as if unperturbed, showing not the slightest fear.
units.literal: Just as various apparitions were emerging from the hall beams, he mounted the ridgepole, singing and shouting as if at ease, utterly without fear.

units.zh: 時有天狗下，乃於其所講武以厭之。
units.en: When a celestial portent appeared, he held military exercises at the spot to ward it off.
units.literal: When the Celestial Dog descended, he performed military drills at that place to counter it.

units.zh: 有兔驚馬，帝墜而絕肋。
units.en: A rabbit startled his horse, and the emperor fell, breaking his ribs.
units.literal: A rabbit startled the horse; the Emperor fell and broke his ribs.

units.zh: 太后視疾，問濟南所在者三，帝不對。
units.en: The empress dowager came to see him in his illness and three times asked where the Prince of Jinan was; the emperor did not reply.
units.literal: The Empress Dowager came to visit him in his illness and three times asked where the Prince of Jinan was; the Emperor did not answer.

units.zh: 太后怒曰：「殺之耶？
units.en: The empress dowager said angrily, "Did you kill him?
units.literal: The Empress Dowager angrily said: "You killed him, did you?

units.zh: 不用吾言，死其宜矣！」
units.en: You refused to listen to me—you deserve to die!"
units.literal: You did not heed my words—death is what you deserve!

units.zh: 臨終之際，唯扶服床枕，叩頭求哀。
units.en: On his deathbed he could only cling to his bed and pillow, kowtowing and pleading for his life.
units.literal: At the point of death he only clung to the bed and pillow, kowtowing and begging for mercy.

units.zh: 遣使詔追長廣王入纂大統，手書云：「宜將吾妻子置一好處，勿學前人也。」
units.en: He dispatched envoys with an edict summoning the Prince of Changguang to succeed him, writing in his own hand: "See that my wife and children are placed somewhere safe; do not do as those before you did."
units.literal: He sent envoys with an edict summoning the Prince of Changguang to succeed to the great succession, writing in his own hand: "You should place my wife and children in a good place; do not imitate those before you."

units.zh: 論曰：神武平定四方，威權在己，遷鄴之後，雖主器有人，號令所加，政皆自出。
units.en: Commentary: Emperor Shenwu pacified the realm and kept power firmly in his own hands. After the capital was moved to Ye, though a sovereign sat on the throne, every command and every policy issued from him alone.
units.literal: The commentary says: Emperor Shenwu pacified the four quarters; authority and power were in his own hands. After moving the capital to Ye, although the heir held the vessel of state, every order issued and every policy enacted came from himself.

units.zh: 文宣因循鴻業，內外葉從，自朝及野，群心屬望，東魏之地，舉國樂推，曾未期月，遂登宸極。
units.en: Emperor Wenxuan inherited this great enterprise; court and country fell into step, and from the capital to the provinces all looked to him. Throughout Eastern Wei the people rallied to his cause, and within a month he had taken the throne.
units.literal: Wenxuan followed the great enterprise; inside and outside were in harmony; from court to countryside all hearts looked to him; throughout the lands of Eastern Wei the whole nation gladly supported him, and within less than a month he ascended the imperial throne.

units.zh: 始則存心政事，風化肅然，數年之間，朝野安出。
units.en: At first he applied himself diligently to governance, and discipline prevailed; within a few years the realm was at peace.
units.literal: At first he devoted his heart to affairs of government and customs were sternly ordered; within a few years court and countryside were secure and at ease.

units.zh: 其後縱酒肆欲，事極倡狂，昏邪殘暴，近代未有，饗國不永，實由斯疾。
units.en: Later he gave himself over to wine and licentiousness to the point of madness—confused, wicked, cruel, and violent as few rulers in memory had been. His reign was brief, and the fault lay in this very failing.
units.literal: Afterward he indulged in wine and unrestrained desire, affairs reaching the extreme of reckless abandon; muddled, depraved, cruel, and violent—unmatched in recent times—his enjoyment of the state was not long; this was truly due to this malady.

units.zh: 濟南繼業，大革其弊，風教粲然，搢紳稱幸。
units.en: The Prince of Jinan succeeded him and vigorously reformed these abuses; culture and morals flourished anew, and the gentry spoke of their good fortune.
units.literal: The Prince of Jinan succeeded to the enterprise and greatly reformed its abuses; customs and teaching shone brightly, and officials and gentry spoke of their good fortune.

units.zh: 股肱輔弼，雖懷厥誠，旣不能贊弘道德，和睦親懿，又不能遠慮防身，深謀衛主，應斷不斷，自取其咎。
units.en: His chief ministers, for all their loyalty, could neither promote virtue and harmony among the imperial kin, nor forestall danger or counsel their lord with far-sighted care. Where decisive action was needed, they failed to act—and brought disaster on themselves.
units.literal: His chief ministers and assistants, though cherishing their loyalty, were neither able to help expand virtue and morality and harmonize kin and in-laws, nor able to plan far ahead to protect themselves and deeply counsel to guard their lord; where they should have acted decisively they did not, and brought ruin upon themselves.

units.zh: 臣旣誅夷，君壽廢辱，皆任非其器之所致爾。
units.en: Ministers were put to death and the sovereign's life ended in humiliation—all because the wrong men had been placed in office.
units.literal: Ministers were executed and the ruler's life cut short in disgrace—all caused by appointing men unfit for their posts.

units.zh: 孝昭早居臺閤，故事通明，人吏之間，無所不委。
units.en: Emperor Xiaozhao had long served in the imperial secretariat, knew its precedents inside out, and was entrusted with every matter great and small.
units.literal: Xiaozhao early occupied the Terrace Pavilion; he was thoroughly versed in precedent; between men and officials nothing was not entrusted to him.

units.zh: 文宣崩後，大革前弊。
units.en: After Emperor Wenxuan's death he undertook sweeping reforms of earlier abuses.
units.literal: After Wenxuan's death he greatly reformed previous abuses.

units.zh: 及臨尊極，留心更深，時人服其明而識其細也。
units.en: Once he ascended the throne his attentiveness only deepened; contemporaries admired his clarity of mind and noted his eye for detail.
units.literal: When he reached the supreme dignity his attention went deeper still; men of the time admired his clarity and recognized his meticulousness.

units.zh: 情好稽古，率由禮度，將封先代之胤，且敦學校之風，徵召英賢，文武畢集。
units.en: He cherished antiquity and governed by ritual propriety; he planned to ennoble descendants of earlier dynasties, revive the culture of learning, and summon men of talent until scholars and soldiers alike had gathered at court.
units.literal: In sentiment he loved antiquity and followed ritual norms; he was about to enfeoff descendants of former dynasties and also promote the spirit of schools, summoning worthy talents until civil and military men were all gathered.

units.zh: 于時周氏朝政移於宰臣，主將相猜，不無危殆。
units.en: At that time power in the Northern Zhou court had passed to its chief ministers; ruler and generals eyed one another with suspicion, and peril was never far away.
units.literal: At that time the Zhou court's governance had shifted to its chief ministers; lord and generals were mutually suspicious, and danger was not absent.

units.zh: 乃眷關右，實懷兼併之志，經謀宏遠，實當代之明主，而降年不永，其故何哉？
units.en: He then looked westward beyond the Pass, harboring real designs of conquest; his plans were bold and far-reaching—he was truly a ruler of rare ability in his time—yet his life was cut short. What was the cause?
units.literal: He then turned his gaze to the lands west of the Pass, truly harboring ambitions of annexation; his plans were far-reaching—he was truly an enlightened ruler of his age—yet his allotted years were not long; what was the reason?

units.zh: 豈幽顯之間，實有報復，將齊之基宇止在於斯，帝欲大之，天不許也？
units.en: Was there retribution at work between the seen and unseen worlds—and was the Northern Qi destined to rise no higher? He sought to expand its domain, but Heaven would not allow it.
units.literal: Was it that between the hidden and the manifest there is truly retribution, and that the foundation of Qi would extend no further—he wished to enlarge it, but Heaven would not permit it?

units.zh: 太皇太后密與孝昭及諸大將定策誅之，下令廢立。
units.en: The Grand Empress Dowager secretly joined Gao Yan and the great generals in fixing a plan to execute them, and issued an edict deposing one ruler and enthroning another.
units.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager secretly joined Xiaozhao and the great generals in fixing a plan to execute them, and issued an edict deposing and enthroning.

units.zh: 孝昭帝崩，太后又下詔立武成帝。
units.en: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, the empress dowager again issued an edict enthroning Emperor Wucheng.
units.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, the empress dowager again issued an edict enthroning Emperor Wucheng.

units.zh: 孝昭即位，復為皇太后。
units.en: When Gao Yan succeeded, she again became Empress Dowager.
units.literal: When Xiaozhao succeeded, she again became Empress Dowager.

units.zh: 孕孝昭則夢蠕龍於地；
units.en: when she conceived Gao Yan she dreamed of a writhing dragon upon the ground;
units.literal: when she conceived Xiaozhao she dreamed of a writhing dragon upon the ground;

units.zh: 孝昭即位，立為皇后。
units.en: When Xiaozhao took the throne, she was installed as empress.
units.literal: When Xiaozhao ascended the throne, she was installed as empress.

units.zh: 武成既殺樂陵王，元被閟隔，不得與家相知。
units.en: After Wucheng killed the Prince of Leling, Empress Yuan was shut away in isolation and could no longer communicate with her family.
units.literal: After Wucheng killed the Prince of Leling, Yuan was shut away and isolated, unable to communicate with her family.

units.zh: 帝崩，梓宮之鄴。
units.en: When the emperor died, his coffin was taken to Ye.
units.literal: When the emperor died, his coffin proceeded to Ye.

units.zh: 孝昭即位，降居昭信宮，號昭信皇后。
units.en: When Gao Yan succeeded, she was reduced to Zhaoxin Palace and styled Empress of Zhaoxin.
units.literal: When Xiaozhao succeeded, she was reduced to Zhaoxin Palace and styled Empress of Zhaoxin.

units.zh: 十一月乙卯，以右丞相、咸陽王斛律金爲左丞相，以錄尚書事、常山王演爲太傅，以司徒、長廣王湛爲太尉，以司空段韶爲司徒，以平陽王淹爲司空，高陽王湜爲尚書左僕射，河間王孝琬爲司州牧，侍中燕子獻爲右僕射。
units.en: In the eleventh month, on the yimao day, Hulu Jin, Prince of Xianyang and right chief minister, was appointed left chief minister; Prince Yan of Changshan, recorder of the Masters of Writing, became grand tutor; Prince Zhan of Changguang, minister over the masses, became grand commandant; Duan Shao, minister of works, became minister over the masses; Prince Yan of Pingyang became minister of works; Prince Shi of Gaoyang became left vice-director of the Masters of Writing; Prince Xiaowan of Hejian became governor of Sizhou; and Yanzi Xian, palace attendant, became right vice-director.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, on the yimao day, the right chief minister, Prince of Xianyang Hulu Jin, was made left chief minister; Prince Yan of Changshan, recorder of the affairs of the Masters of Writing, was made grand tutor; Prince Zhan of Changguang, minister over the masses, was made grand commandant; Duan Shao, minister of works, was made minister over the masses; Prince Yan of Pingyang was made minister of works; Prince Shi of Gaoyang was made left vice-director of the Masters of Writing; Prince Xiaowan of Hejian was made governor of Sizhou; and Yanzi Xian, attendant at the palace, was made right vice-director.

units.zh: 戊申，以常山王演爲大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，以大司馬、長廣王湛爲太傅、京畿大都督，以司徒段韶爲大將軍，以前司空、平陽王淹爲太尉，以司空、平秦王歸彥爲司徒，彭城王浟爲尚書令。
units.en: On the wushen day, Prince Yan of Changshan was appointed grand chief minister, commander of all armies, and recorder of the Masters of Writing. Prince Zhan of Changguang, grand marshal, became grand tutor and metropolitan commander of the capital region. Duan Shao, minister over the masses, became great general; Prince Yan of Pingyang, formerly minister of works, became grand commandant; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, minister of works, became minister over the masses; and Prince You of Pengcheng became director of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: On the wushen day, Prince Yan of Changshan was made grand chief minister, commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, and recorder of the affairs of the Masters of Writing; Prince Zhan of Changguang, grand marshal, was made grand tutor and metropolitan commander of the capital region; Duan Shao, minister over the masses, was made great general; the former minister of works, Prince Yan of Pingyang, was made grand commandant; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, minister of works, was made minister over the masses; and Prince You of Pengcheng was made director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 其長史慕容紹宗諫曰：「不可，今四方擾擾，人懷異望，況高公雄略，又握大兵，將不可為。」
units.en: His chief secretary Murong Shaozong warned, "You cannot do this. The realm is in turmoil and men turn their hopes elsewhere; Gao Huan is ambitious and now commands a great army—this cannot stand."
units.literal: His chief clerk Murong Shaozong remonstrated, saying: "It must not be done. Now the four quarters are in turmoil and men harbor divergent hopes; moreover High Duke Gao is heroic in strategy and holds great armies — this will not do."

units.zh: 紹宗曰：「親兄弟尚爾難信，何論香火！」
units.en: Shaozong replied, "Full brothers cannot trust each other—what use is a sworn oath?"
units.literal: Shaozong said: "Even full brothers are thus hard to trust — how much less an oath before incense!"

units.zh: 兆不納，殺帝，而與尒朱世隆等立長廣王曄，改元建明。
units.en: Zhao refused to heed him, killed the emperor, and with Erzhu Shilong and others enthroned Ye, Prince of Changguang, changing the era name to Jianming.
units.literal: Zhao did not accept; he killed the emperor, and with Erzhu Shilong and others enthroned Prince Changguang Ye and changed the era name to Jianming.

units.zh: 時兆左右已受神武金，因譖紹宗與神武舊有隙，兆乃禁紹宗而催神武發。
units.en: By then Zhao's attendants had taken Gao Huan's gold and accused Shaozong of an old feud with Gao Huan; Zhao imprisoned Shaozong and pressed Gao Huan to march.
units.literal: At that time those at Zhao's side had already received Shenwu's gold; they therefore slandered Shaozong, saying he and Shenwu had old grudges; Zhao thereupon confined Shaozong and urged Shenwu to depart.

units.zh: 兆聞，乃釋紹宗而問焉。
units.en: When Erzhu Zhao heard, he released Shaozong and asked his meaning.
units.literal: When Zhao heard, he released Shaozong and questioned him.

units.zh: 紹宗曰：「猶掌握中物也。」
units.en: Shaozong said, "It is still something clasped in your palm."
units.literal: Shaozong said: "It is still like something in the palm of the hand."

units.zh: 乙巳，太師、常山王演矯詔誅尚書令楊愔、尚書右僕射燕子獻、領軍大將軍可朱渾天和、侍中宋欽道、散騎常侍鄭子默。
units.en: On the yisi day Prince Yan of Changshan, grand preceptor, forged an edict and had executed Yang Yin, director of the Masters of Writing; Yanzi Xian, right vice-director; Kezhuhun Tianhe, commanding general of the palace guards; Song Qindao, palace attendant; and Zheng Zimo, attendant of the scattered cavalry.
units.literal: On the yisi day the grand preceptor, Prince of Changshan Yan, forged an edict and executed Yang Yin, director of the Masters of Writing; Yanzi Xian, right vice-director of the Masters of Writing; Kezhuhun Tianhe, general-in-chief commanding the guards; Song Qindao, attendant at the palace; and Zheng Zimo, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

units.zh: 万俟普 子 洛 可朱渾元 劉豐 破六韓常 金祚 韋子粲
units.en: Moqi Pu; his son Luo; Kezhuhun Yuan; Liu Feng; Poliuhan Chang; Jin Zuo; Wei Zican
units.literal: Moqi Pu; son Luo; Kezhuhun Yuan; Liu Feng; Poliuhan Chang; Jin Zuo; Wei Zican

units.zh: 破六韓常，字保年，附化人，匈奴單于之裔也。
units.en: Poliuhan Chang, styled Baonian, was a man of Fuhua and a descendant of the Xiongnu shanyu.
units.literal: Poliuhan Chang, styled Baonian, was a man of Fuhua and a descendant of the Xiongnu Shanyu.

units.zh: 常沈敏有膽略，善騎射，累遷平西將軍。
units.en: Chang was deep and keen, bold and resourceful, and skilled in mounted archery; he rose in succession to general who pacifies the west.
units.literal: Chang was deep, keen, and had courage and resource; skilled in mounted archery; he rose in succession to General Who Pacifies the West.

units.zh: 贈尚書令、司徒公、太傅、第一領民酋長，假王，諡曰忠武。
units.en: Posthumously he was made director of the masters of writing, duke of the department of state affairs, grand tutor, and chief of the first tribally enrolled division, with princely rank in title and the posthumous title Loyal and Martial.
units.literal: Posthumously he was given Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Tutor, chief of the first tribally enrolled division, prince in title, posthumous title Zhongwu.

units.zh: 與諸將征討，又從高祖攻擊諸寇，累遷車騎大將軍、開府，封平陽公，除洛州刺史。
units.en: On punitive campaigns with the generals he again followed Gao Huan against the bandits, rising in succession to grand general of chariots and cavalry, opener of a government office, duke of Pingyang, and governor of Luo Province.
units.literal: With the generals on punitive campaigns he again followed Gao Huan in attacking the various bandits, rising in succession to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Opener of a Government Office, Duke of Pingyang, and governor of Luo Province.

units.zh: 高祖起義，常為附化守，與万俟受洛干東歸，高祖嘉之，上為撫軍。
units.en: When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Chang was defender of Fuhua; he returned east with Moqi Shouluogan. Gao Huan praised this and promoted him to military inspector.
units.literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Chang was defender of Fuhua; he returned east with Moqi Shouluogan; Gao Huan praised this and promoted him to Military Inspector.

units.zh: 常秩滿，還晉陽，拜太保、滄州刺史，卒。
units.en: When Chang's term expired he returned to Jinyang, was made grand mentor and governor of Cang Province, and died.
units.literal: When Chang's term expired he returned to Jinyang, was made Grand Mentor and governor of Cang Province, and died.

units.zh: 世領部落，其父孔雀，世襲酋長。
units.en: For generations they led their tribe; his father Kongque had inherited the chieftaincy in turn.
units.literal: For generations they led their tribe; his father Kongque inherited the chieftaincy in succession.

units.zh: 常啟世宗曰：「常自鎮河陽以來，頻出關口，太谷二道，北荊已北，洛州已南，所有要害，頗所知悉。
units.en: Chang addressed Gao Cheng, saying, "Since I garrisoned Heyang I have repeatedly sallied through the passes. Of the two routes through Taiyu, north of Northern Jing and south of Luo Province, I know every strategic point.
units.literal: Chang addressed Gao Cheng, saying: "Since I have garrisoned Heyang, I have repeatedly sallied through the passes. Of the two routes through Taiyu, north of Northern Jing and south of Luo Province, I know well all the strategic points.

units.zh: 世宗納其計，遣大司馬斛律金等築楊志、百家、呼延三鎮。
units.en: Gao Cheng adopted his plan and sent Grand Marshal Hulü Jin and others to build the three garrisons of Yangzhi, Baijia, and Huyan.
units.literal: Gao Cheng adopted his plan and sent Grand Marshal Hulü Jin and others to build the three garrisons of Yangzhi, Baijia, and Huyan.

units.zh: 右谷蠡王潘六奚沒於魏，其子孫以潘六奚為氏，後人訛誤，以為破六韓。
units.en: The right kuuli prince Pan Liuxi perished in Wei; his descendants took Pan Liuxi as their clan name, and later men garbled it into Poliuhan.
units.literal: Right kuuli prince Pan Liuxi perished in Wei; his descendants took Pan Liuxi as their clan name; later men garbled it into Poliuhan.

units.zh: 時宗人拔陵為亂，以孔雀為大都督、司徒、平南王。
units.en: At that time their clansman Baling raised rebellion and made Kongque grand commander of the north, director of state affairs, and prince who pacifies the south.
units.literal: At that time their clansman Baling raised rebellion and made Kongque grand commander of the north, Director of State Affairs, and Prince Who Pacifies the South.

units.zh: 而太谷南口去荊路逾一百，經赤工阪，是賊往還東西大道，中間曠絕一百五十里，賊之糧饢，唯經此路。
units.en: Yet the southern mouth of Taiyu lies more than a hundred li from the Jing route, passes Chigong Slope, and is the bandits' chief east-west thoroughfare. Between them lies open country a hundred and fifty li across; the bandits' grain and fodder must come only by this road.
units.literal: Yet the southern mouth of Taiyu lies more than a hundred li from the Jing route, passes Chigong Slope, and is the bandits' chief east-west thoroughfare. In the middle lies open country of a hundred and fifty li; the bandits' grain and fodder must come only by this road.

units.zh: 愚謂於彼選形勝之處，營築城戍，安置士馬，截其遠還，自然不能更有行送。」
units.en: I humbly propose that we choose a place of natural advantage there, build garrison walls, station troops and horses, and cut their long supply line — then naturally they could no longer send convoys."
units.literal: I humbly propose selecting a place of natural advantage there, building garrison walls, stationing troops and horses, and cutting off their long supply line — then naturally they could no longer send convoys."

units.zh: 東魏陝州刺史劉貴以步騎千餘邀之。
units.en: Liu Gui, Eastern Wei's governor of Shan province, intercepted him with more than a thousand foot and horse.
units.literal: Liu Gui, Governor of Shan Province of Eastern Wei, with more than a thousand infantry and cavalry intercepted him.

units.zh: 世祖武成皇帝，諱湛，神武皇帝第九子，孝昭皇帝之母弟也。
units.en: Emperor Wucheng, Gao Zhan, posthumous title Shizu, was the ninth son of Emperor Shenwu and the full younger brother of Emperor Xiaozhao.
units.literal: Emperor Wucheng, posthumous title Shizu, taboo name Zhan, was the ninth son of Emperor Shenwu and the younger brother of Emperor Xiaozhao by the same mother.

units.zh: 天統四年十二月辛未，太上皇帝崩於鄴宮乾壽堂，時年三十二，諡曰武成皇帝，廟號世祖。
units.en: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of the Tiantong era, on the xinwei day, the retired emperor died in the Qianshou Hall of the Ye Palace. He was thirty-two years old. He was posthumously titled Emperor Wucheng, with the temple name Shizu.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Tiantong, on the xinwei day, the retired emperor died in the Qianshou Hall of the Ye Palace. He was thirty-two years old. His posthumous title was Emperor Wucheng, and his temple name was Shizu.

units.zh: 於是群公上尊號為太上皇帝，軍國大事咸以奏聞。
units.en: The lords then offered him the title Retired Emperor, and all major military and state affairs continued to be submitted to him.
units.literal: Thereupon the assembled lords presented him with the honorific title Retired Emperor, and all great affairs of the army and state were reported to him.

units.zh: 大寧元年冬十一月癸丑，皇帝即位於南宮，大赦，改皇建二年為大寧。
units.en: In winter, in the eleventh month of the first year of Daning, on guichou, the emperor took the throne in the Southern Palace, proclaimed a general amnesty, and renamed the second year of Huangjian as Daning.
units.literal: In the first year of Daning, in winter, in the eleventh month, on the guichou day, the emperor ascended the throne in the Southern Palace, issued a general amnesty, and changed the second year of Huangjian to Daning.

units.zh: 丙子，乃使太宰段韶兼太尉，持節奉皇帝璽綬傳位於皇太子，大赦，改元為天統元年，百官進級降罪各有差。
units.en: On bingzi, Grand Minister Duan Shao, concurrently Grand Commandant, was sent with the credentials to convey the imperial seals and ribbons and transfer the throne to the crown prince. A general amnesty was proclaimed, the era was changed to Tiantong, and officials were advanced and punishments reduced by graded degrees.
units.literal: On the bingzi day, he then had the Grand Minister Duan Shao concurrently serve as Grand Commandant and, bearing the credentials, present the imperial seals and ribbons to transmit the throne to the crown prince; a general amnesty was proclaimed, the era name was changed to the first year of Tiantong, and the hundred officials were advanced in grade and punishments reduced, each by rank.

units.zh: 元象中，封長廣郡公。
units.en: During the Yuanxiang era, he was made Duke of Changguang Commandery.
units.literal: During the Yuanxiang era, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Changguang Commandery.

units.zh: 天保初，進爵為王，拜尚書令，尋兼司徒，遷太尉。
units.en: At the opening of the Tianbao era, he was raised to princely rank, made Chief Minister of the Secretariat, soon also given concurrent appointment as Minister over the Masses, and then transferred to Grand Commander.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, his rank was advanced to prince; he was appointed Chief Minister of the Secretariat, soon also served concurrently as Minister over the Masses, and was transferred to Grand Commander.

units.zh: 神武方招懷荒遠，乃為帝聘蠕蠕太子庵羅辰女，號「鄰和公主」。
units.en: While Emperor Shenwu was working to bring distant peoples into allegiance, he betrothed the prince to the daughter of Anluochen, the Rouran crown prince, who was given the title "Princess Linhe."
units.literal: When Shenwu was seeking to win over distant frontier peoples, he arranged a marriage for the Emperor with the daughter of Anluochen, heir of the Rouran crown prince, titled "Princess Linhe."

units.zh: 丙戌，立妃胡氏為皇后，子緯為皇太子。
units.en: On bingxu, Consort Hu was made empress and his son Wei was made crown prince.
units.literal: On the bingxu day, he established Consort Hu as empress and his son Wei as crown prince.

units.zh: 秋九月乙丑，封皇子綽為南陽王，儼為東平王。
units.en: In the ninth month of autumn, on the yichou day, the princes Chuo and Yan were enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang and Prince of Dongping, respectively.
units.literal: In the ninth month of autumn, on the yichou day, the emperor's sons Chuo and Yan were enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang and Prince of Dongping, respectively.

units.zh: 帝時年八歲，冠服端嚴，神情閑遠，華戎歎異。
units.en: The prince was then eight years old. His dress was dignified and his manner calm and composed, and both Chinese and foreigners alike expressed admiration.
units.literal: At the time the Emperor was eight years old; his cap and robes were dignified, his expression serene and distant, and both Chinese and barbarians marveled.

units.zh: 乾明初，楊愔等密相疏忌，以帝為大司馬，領幷州刺史。
units.en: At the start of the Qianming era, Yang Yin and his faction secretly kept their distance and were wary of him, but nevertheless made him Grand Marshal and Inspector of Bing Province.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianming, Yang Yin and others secretly kept their distance and were wary of him, and appointed the Emperor Grand Marshal with concurrent duty as Inspector of Bing Province.

units.zh: 帝旣與孝昭謀誅諸執政，遷太傅、錄尚書事、領京畿大都督。
units.en: After he and Emperor Xiaozhao plotted to execute the ruling ministers, he was made Grand Tutor, Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat, and Metropolitan Commander of the Capital Region.
units.literal: Once the Emperor had joined with Xiaozhao in plotting to execute the ruling ministers, he was transferred to Grand Tutor, Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat, and Metropolitan Commander of the Capital Region.

units.zh: 皇建初，進位右丞相。
units.en: At the opening of the Huangjian era, he was promoted to Right Chancellor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was promoted to Right Chancellor.

units.zh: 丁巳，帝自晉陽南討。
units.en: On dingsi, the emperor set out south from Jinyang on campaign.
units.literal: On the dingsi day, the emperor went south from Jinyang to campaign.

units.zh: 論曰：武成風度高爽，經算弘長，文武之官，俱盡其力，有帝王之量矣。
units.en: The appraisal says: Wucheng had an elevated bearing and far-reaching strategic judgment. Civil and military officials alike gave him their full efforts, and he possessed the measure of an emperor.
units.literal: The appraisal says: Wucheng's bearing was lofty and expansive, and his plans and calculations were broad and far-reaching; civil and military officials all exerted their full efforts for him, and he had the capacity of an emperor.

units.zh: 但愛狎庸豎，委以朝權，帷薄之間，淫侈過度，滅亡之兆，其在斯乎？
units.en: Yet he was intimate with base underlings and entrusted them with court power, while within the palace chambers his licentious extravagance exceeded all bounds. The signs of ruin lay precisely there, did they not?
units.literal: Yet he loved and kept close company with mediocre underlings, entrusted them with power at court, and in the inner chambers indulged in licentious extravagance beyond measure; were the signs of destruction not here?

units.zh: 玄象告變，傳位元子，名號雖殊，政猶己出，跡有虛飾，事非憲典，聰明臨下，何易可誣。
units.en: Celestial signs announced change, so he passed the throne to his eldest son. The title changed, but government still came from him; the act was empty ornament, not proper precedent. With Heaven watching clearly from above, it could hardly be deceived.
units.literal: The dark celestial signs announced change, and he transmitted the throne to his eldest son; although the title and name were different, government still issued from himself. The act had empty ornament and was not in accord with constitutional precedent; with Heaven's clear intelligence looking down below, it could hardly be deceived.
